description: r7-sched — authored through the bareloop panel (green, js)

jobLines.text: Fix the bug in src/sum.js so the tests in test/sum.test.js pass

goal: Fix the bug in src/sum.js so that `node --test test/sum.test.js` reports all its tests passing, with no new dependencies added to the package and the files changed only under src/.

notes: The confirmed plan's second check — 'package.json dependencies/devDependencies unchanged from the seed, and no lockfile or node_modules appeared' — has NO stage. I could not express it with the kinds available: the seed tree listing is only package.json, src, test (no lockfile, no node_modules, so there is no seed path to measure a lockfile count against), and I have no read-only parsing of package.json that is not also a new command I would have to invent. Nesting it under the changed-from-seed guard's allowPrefixes (src/) would only partially help: any write to package.json, a lockfile or node_modules is already outside src/ and therefore already refused by the write fence, which is why I did not add a stage for it. If the person wants it explicit, the write fence is the check that covers it.

NOT CHECKED, per the person's own list: test/sum.test.js being left untouched or the tests not being weakened — I only check that the suite passes and that no more/fewer tests execute; the fix inside src/sum.js being a general fix rather than a special case that satisfies the two tests; the ticket at https://github.com/hamr0/hol-guard/issues (its URL is the only ticket input, and no priority or label is named anywhere in the job, so there is no ticketFilter and no ticket-content stage).

No typecheck stage exists and none is composed: the survey found no tsconfig.json, no jsconfig.json, no typescript dependency and no lint script, so there is no checker to run. The genre's typecheck/typecheck-outside stages would be instruments pointing at nothing here.

Tests are invoked as `node --test test/sum.test.js` from the package root, the command the survey read off package.json scripts.test; node is the language module runner for this ESM package ("type": "module"), and the test file uses explicit .js specifiers.

The TAP patterns (# tests / # fail) are the genre's measured node-test-total-count and node-test-fail-count spellings, read as figures with aggregate 'first'; Node prints both counters on every run including a green one, so a green zero is a reported zero, not an unreported one. The 'suite-green' stage is the exit-code half of the same assertion.

The scope objects on the two counting stages name which population they count (the single test file), not a path inside lineMatch, so a clean run matches the TAP line rather than losing the instrument.
